## 1. UUIDs the client knows about

`ble_sensor.c:71-89`:
```c
#define UUID_HRS                0x180Du
#define UUID_CSCS               0x1816u
#define UUID_CPS                0x1818u
#define UUID_BAS                0x180Fu
#define UUID_HR_MEAS            0x2A37u
#define UUID_CSC_MEAS           0x2A5Bu
#define UUID_CP_MEAS            0x2A63u
#define UUID_BAT_LEVEL          0x2A19u
#define UUID_BODY_SENSOR_LOC    0x2A38u
...
#define SENSOR_KIND_HR          0
#define SENSOR_KIND_CSC         1
#define SENSOR_KIND_CPS         2
#define SENSOR_FEAT_HR          (1u << 0)
#define SENSOR_FEAT_CSC         (1u << 1)
#define SENSOR_FEAT_CPS         (1u << 2)
#define SENSOR_FEAT_BAT         (1u << 3)
#define SENSOR_FEAT_LOC         (1u << 4)
```

**There is no `0x2A5C` (CSC Feature), no `0x2A5D` (Sensor Location), and no `0x2A55` (SC Control Point) anywhere in the firmware client.** I grepped the whole `my_vendor` tree and `frameworks/ packages/ apps/ external/`: those UUIDs appear only in the ESP-IDF `blecsc` example and in the SiFli SDK header (see §4). Likewise there is no SC Control Point write, no Set Cumulative Wheel Revolutions (0x01), no Start Calibration (0x02). Cycling Power is handled, but only 0x1818 service + 0x2A63 notify measurement.

---

## 2. What the client does on discovery

### 2.1 It is deliberately UUID-targeted, never discover-all

`ble_sensor.c:3602-3605` (in the `SENSOR_DISCOVERING` pump case):
```c
su = (slot->disc_step == 0) ?
     UUID_BAS : kind_svc_uuid(slot->kind);
uuid = BT_UUID_DECLARE_16(su);
if (bt_gattc_discover_service(slot->gatt, &uuid) != BT_STATUS_SUCCESS)
```
Two rounds: first `0x180F` (BAS, optional), then `0x1816` for the CSC slot. `SENSOR_DISCOVER_DELAY_MS = 500u` (:98) is waited after connect before the first round. The board SAL keeps the discovered table across the second discovers (`keep_db`), and on table overflow reports failure instead of letting SAL HCI-disconnect (`sal_gatt_client_interface.c:191,201`; sizing `GATT_CLIENT_SERVICE_MAX=8`, `ELEMENT_MAX=40`, `CHAR_PER_SERVICE_MAX=16` in `configs/nsh/defconfig:148-150`).

### 2.2 It aborts the link if 0x1816 is missing — yes

`ble_sensor.c:1816-1822`:
```c
if ((slot->feat & kind_feat_bit(slot->kind)) == 0)
  {
    LOGE("%s discover missing 0x%04x", kind_name(slot->kind),
         (unsigned)kind_svc_uuid(slot->kind));
    slot->drop_link = true;
    return;
  }
```
`slot->feat` is set from the *service* UUID seen during that discover (`:1781-1788`, `u16 == UUID_CSCS` → `SENSOR_FEAT_CSC`), so **the primary service 0x1816 must be present in the ATT database**, otherwise the client sets `drop_link` and disconnects (`:3718-3723`).

### 2.3 It requires the measurement characteristic 0x2A5B and a working NOTIFY CCC

`ble_sensor.c:2796-2808`:
```c
if (slot->sub_step == 0)
  {
    if (slot_subscribe_uuid(slot, kind_meas_uuid(slot->kind)))
      { return; }
    LOGE("%s meas CCC missing", kind_name(slot->kind));
    slot->drop_link = true;
    return;
  }
```
`slot_subscribe_uuid()` :2695-2723 does `bt_gattc_get_attribute_by_uuid(slot->gatt, 0x0001, 0xffff, &uuid, &desc)` over the **whole handle space** and then:
```c
ret = bt_gattc_subscribe(slot->gatt, desc.handle, GATT_CCC_NOTIFY);
```
So: standard UUID 0x2A5B, and it must accept a CCC *notify* subscription (value 0x0001). Notify, not indicate. `SENSOR_SUB_RETRY_MAX = 3` failures → `drop_link` (`:1864-1868`); `SENSOR_CONNECT_MS = 15000` bounds every stage.

### 2.4 What it reads: 0x2A19 and **0x2A38**, not 0x2A5C/0x2A5D

`slot_subscribe_next()` :2827-2833:
```c
slot_read_loc(slot);
if (slot->bat_h != 0)
  { (void)bt_gattc_read(slot->gatt, slot->bat_h); }
slot_finish_ready(slot);
```
`slot_read_loc()` :2776-2789 reads **`UUID_BODY_SENSOR_LOC = 0x2A38`** (the HR body-sensor-location, harmless if absent). Battery `0x2A19` is CCC-subscribed if it has Notify, otherwise polled every 2000 ms (`SENSOR_POLL_MS`, :3663-3665). Nothing is ever written to the sensor except CCCs — **no writes to any characteristic**.

READY is only reached if `slot->meas_sub_ok` is true (:2820-2825, `"CSC meas CCC not armed"` → `drop_link`), and reaching READY is what persists the binding record (`slot_finish_ready` :1268-1292).

### 2.5 Exact CSC Measurement (0x2A5B) layout it parses

`parse_csc_meas()` :1359-1412, verbatim (comments trimmed):
```c
  flags = p[0];
  if ((flags & 0x01) != 0)
    { off = (uint16_t)(off + 6); }      /* off starts at 1 */

  if ((flags & 0x02) == 0)
    { return; }                          /* crank data REQUIRED */

  if ((uint16_t)(off + 4) > len)
    { return; }

  crank_revs = (uint16_t)(p[off] | ((uint16_t)p[off + 1] << 8));
  crank_time = (uint16_t)(p[off + 2] | ((uint16_t)p[off + 3] << 8));

  if (slot->csc_have)
    {
      uint16_t drev  = (uint16_t)(crank_revs - slot->crank_revs);
      uint16_t dtime = (uint16_t)(crank_time - slot->crank_time);

      if (drev > 0 && dtime > 0)
        {
          uint32_t rpm = ((uint32_t)drev * 1024u * 60u) / dtime;
          if (rpm > 0 && rpm < 300)
            {
              slot->last_csc_rpm = (uint16_t)rpm;
              slot->meas_idle    = false;
              companion_bridge_sensor_set_cadence((uint16_t)rpm, now_ms);
            }
        }
    }
```
Conclusions for the simulator, all load-bearing:

- **Byte-for-byte per spec, no vendor quirk.** flags bit0 (wheel revs present) → skip exactly 6 bytes (4-byte cumulative wheel revs LE + 2-byte last wheel event time LE); flags bit1 (crank revs present) → 16-bit LE cumulative crank revs, then 16-bit LE last crank event time in 1/1024 s units. The RPM math is spec-correct: `drev * 1024 * 60 / dtime`.
- **flags bit1 must be set.** If you only send wheel data, the client silently returns — a "cadence meter" that advertises CSC but sends no crank field will look alive-but-dead.
- Total length: `len >= 11` when wheel data is present, `len >= 5` when only crank data.
- **Deltas matter, so the first notification only seeds the baseline** (`csc_have`). Send at least two. `drev == 0` publishes nothing (so true 0 rpm is unrepresentable — the UI shows `idle` after 8 s instead). **`rpm >= 300` is discarded**, and rpm is integer-divided.
- A `BT_AD_SERVICE_DATA16` (AD type 0x16) element with UUID 0x1816 is *also* parsed as a measurement straight from the advert (`walk_ad` :1573-1578), into the CSC slot's baseline. You do not need this, but it means advert service-data will perturb the delta baseline before connect.
- No CRC/sequence checking, no temporal sanity check — a wrap of the 16-bit counters is handled naturally by unsigned subtraction.

For completeness, Cycling Power `parse_cps_meas()` :1417-1445 has a **quirk**: it hardcodes `watts = (int16_t)(p[2] | (p[3] << 8))` and `len >= 4`, i.e. it assumes the **Pedal Power Balance byte is present (flags bit0 set)**. If your sim sends CPS, send flags `0x01` + 1 dummy balance byte, then instantaneous power LE (which is also what many real meters do). Negative → clamped to 0; `> 3000` W → dropped.

---

## 3. Scan / connect path and the preconditions your peripheral must satisfy

### 3.1 No name filter, no MAC hardcoding — address-only, from an advert

- Device selection is by **16-bit service UUID in the ADV** for the discovery list (`walk_ad` :1540-1562 matches `BT_AD_UUID16_SOME/ALL`; `on_scan_result` :2166 requires `svc_mask != 0` and `rssi >= SENSOR_RSSI_MIN = -90`).
- Connect is **by address only**. The comment at :1509 states it explicitly: `连接绝不按名：是否入表由 UUID 掩码决定`. There is no `strstr`/name prefix anywhere in `ble_sensor.c`.
- Auto-reconnect (`autorc`) requires watching for the **saved address** and does *not* require the UUID in the ADV — but `slot_try_connect()` only runs when `slot->adv_seen` was set by an ADV from that exact address (`:2426-2430`, `slot_try_connect` :2908+).
- Manual selection path `ble_sensor_connect_index_kind()` :2218+: rejects with `"connect idx=%u: no %s service in ADV"` if the ADV lacks the requested service; **you must put 0x1816 in the advert** (`Flags + Complete/Incomplete List of 16-bit Service UUIDs`, or service data) or the menu can't bind it. One address = one GATTC slot: a device advertising both 0x1816 and 0x1818 will trip `"%s busy with another %s"`.

### 3.2 Address stability — the single biggest trap (documented at length)

`docs/ble/ble_sensor.md` §3.11 (:266-327) records the field failure and the decision:
> `**改用 ESP32 做模拟器**：把地址设成**静态随机/public**（高两位 `11`），现有 `autorc` 逻辑立刻正确工作，一行固件都不用改。`

Rule table from :274-279: first-byte top two bits `11` = static random/public (**stable** — required); `01` = resolvable private address (**rotates**, no IRK binding exists in this build: `有 SMP/PRIVACY，无 BT_SETTINGS`); `00` = non-resolvable; `10` = reserved (what the phone app's UI displayed). The old phone-app simulator rotated RPAs (`47:08:D7:18:AD:F4 → 7B:EB:BA:12:F7:BD → …`), so `autorc` never matched. `addr_eq()` compares only the 6 bytes, ignoring `type` (:475-482).

Note the ESP-IDF `blecsc` example already does the right thing: `ble_hs_id_infer_auto(0, &blecsc_addr_type)` with `privacy = 0` picks from `{BLE_OWN_ADDR_RANDOM, BLE_OWN_ADDR_PUBLIC}` (nimble `ble_hs_id.c:411-433`), i.e. a **static random** address if one is set, else public. Either is stable and satisfies the rule.

### 3.3 Connectable advertising is mandatory and must stop after connect

- `adv_is_connectable()` :956-964 excludes NONCONN_IND / SCAN_RSP variants. The zombie detector :2196-2214 requires a *connectable* ADV while the slot is `SENSOR_READY`/`SUBSCRIBING` **and** the link is judged not alive (`slot_link_alive`: no measurement notify and no battery within 8 s), `SENSOR_HEALTH_ADV_HITS = 2` hits → `drop_link`, log `"%s advertised while linked (zombie), reconnect"`. Practical rule: **stop advertising on connect** (or the client will eventually tear you down whenever notifications pause).
- No directed advertising is used or needed. `pairing_and_radio.md:76-84` explains why directed ADV was abandoned generally (rotating RPAs of the peer, and no discoverability gain).
- The client scans **legacy, passive, 1M** (`sensor_start_scan` :2384-2391, `scan_type = BT_LE_SCAN_TYPE_PASSIVE`), so active scan responses are never solicited — your SCAN_RSP will not be read. Only ADV_IND payload matters.
- The client connects with `BT_LE_CONN_PARAM_DEFAULT` and never forces 7.5 ms / PHY / DLE on the sensor (:2905-2906 doc comment); accept whatever it proposes, it will be ~30-50 ms with a 4 s supervision timeout.

### 3.4 Radio time-slicing — your advertising must be findable inside a 1 s window

`ble_sensor.c:117-119` + `:2623-2655`:
```c
#define SENSOR_PHONE_ADV_WINDOW_MS   2000u
#define SENSOR_RECONNECT_SCAN_MS     1000u
```
When the phone is not connected and a sensor is wanted but not seen, the single radio alternates `ADV_WINDOW(2000 ms) → ADV_STOP_WAIT → SCAN_WINDOW(1000 ms) → …`, and an empty scan round lengthens the *next phone ADV window* by 2/4/8/16 s up to +32 s. The scan window itself stays 1 s. So with a slow or unlucky advertising interval you can wait up to ~32 s between being listened for. Use a fast interval (the ESP-IDF example's default 30-60 ms is fine; anything well under 1 s with a handful of repeats is fine). Directed/periodic advertising is not usable. `slot_try_connect()` also **waits for the "phone advertising stopped" acknowledgement** before initiating (`SENSOR_ADV_STOP_ACK_MS = 1500`, :2987-3003) — that's a client-side pacing rule, nothing your peripheral must do, but it adds latency you'll see in logs as `<kind> wait adv-stop ack before initiate`.

### 3.5 Requirements on the parked state (stop of pedaling)

The client tolerates a CSC sensor that stops notifying (docs §3.3 :88): CSC/CPS staleness for 8 s only sets `meas_idle = true` (:3701-3704, silent, no log), keeps the GATT link, and probes liveness with ATT reads. `slot_idle_link_check()` :2841-2900 picks the read handle:
```c
h = slot->bat_h != 0 ? slot->bat_h :
    (slot->csc_h != 0 ? slot->csc_h :
     (slot->cps_h != 0 ? slot->cps_h : slot->hr_h));
```
So on a battery-less CSC sensor the client will **ATT-read the 0x2A5B handle**. {"content": "/* BLE Cycling Speed and Cadence service - the parts a cadence-only sensor uses.
 *
 * Values are from the adopted CSCS profile (service 0x1816).  They are spelled
 * out here instead of using NimBLE's service headers because those live outside
 * the public include path.
 */
#ifndef CSC_DEFS_H
#define CSC_DEFS_H

/* --- Service 0x1816: Cycling Speed and Cadence ------------------------- */
#define UUID_CSC_SVC    0x1816
#define UUID_CSC_MEAS   0x2A5B  /* CSC Measurement      : notify (+ read) */
#define UUID_CSC_FEAT   0x2A5C  /* CSC Feature          : read            */
#define UUID_CSC_LOC    0x2A5D  /* Sensor Location      : read            */
#define UUID_CSC_CP     0x2A55  /* SC Control Point     : write, indicate */

/* CSC Measurement, byte 0 */
#define CSC_MEAS_FLAG_WHEEL_REV   0x01  /* 4 B wheel revs + 2 B wheel event time follow */
#define CSC_MEAS_FLAG_CRANK_REV   0x02  /* 2 B crank revs + 2 B crank event time follow */

/* CSC Feature, 16 bit little endian */
#define CSC_FEAT_WHEEL_REV_DATA   0x0001
#define CSC_FEAT_CRANK_REV_DATA   0x0002
#define CSC_FEAT_MULTI_SENSOR_LOC 0x0004

/* Sensor Location (0x2A5D) */
#define CSC_LOC_OTHER         0x00
#define CSC_LOC_LEFT_CRANK    0x05
#define CSC_LOC_RIGHT_CRANK   0x06
#define CSC_LOC_CHAINSTAY     0x0B
#define CSC_LOC_REAR_HUB      0x0D

/* SC Control Point (0x2A55) op codes */
#define CSC_CP_OP_SET_WHEEL_REVS        0x01
#define CSC_CP_OP_START_CALIBRATION     0x02
#define CSC_CP_OP_UPDATE_SENSOR_LOC     0x03
#define CSC_CP_OP_REQ_SUPPORTED_LOCS    0x04
#define CSC_CP_OP_RESPONSE              0x10

/* SC Control Point response values (CSCS 1.0.1, table 3.6) */
#define CSC_CP_RESP_SUCCESS             0x01
#define CSC_CP_RESP_OP_NOT_SUPPORTED    0x02
#define CSC_CP_RESP_INVALID_PARAM       0x03
#define CSC_CP_RESP_OPERATION_FAILED    0x04
#define CSC_CP_RESP_CCC_IMPROPERLY_CFG  0x05

/* ATT error used by this profile when the control point indication CCC is off */
#define CSC_ATT_ERR_CCC_IMPROPERLY_CFG  0x81

/* --- Service 0x180F: Battery, service 0x180A: Device Information -------- */
#define UUID_BAS_SVC    0x180F
#define UUID_BAS_LEVEL  0x2A19  /* Battery Level : read, notify */

#define UUID_DIS_SVC    0x180A
#define UUID_DIS_MANUF   0x2A29
#define UUID_DIS_MODEL   0x2A24
#define UUID_DIS_FW_REV  0x2A26

#endif /* CSC_DEFS_H */

    args = ap.parse_args()

    s = serial.Serial()
    s.port = args.port
    s.baudrate = args.baud
    s.dtr = False
    s.rts = False
    s.timeout = 0.1
    s.open()

    def pump(seconds):
        end = time.time() + seconds
        out = b""
        while time.time() < end:
            chunk = s.read(4096)
            if chunk:
                out += chunk
                sys.stdout.write(chunk.decode("utf-8", "replace"))
                sys.stdout.flush()
        return out

    if args.reset:
        s.setRTS(True)
        time.sleep(0.15)
        s.setRTS(False)
        time.sleep(0.05)

    if args.read:
        pump(args.read)

    for cmd in args.cmd:
        s.write((cmd + "\r\n").encode())
        s.flush()
        print("\n--- %s ---" % cmd)
        pump(1.5 if cmd in ("status", "help") else 2.5)

    s.close()

{"content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Reference CSC central on the bench host (BlueZ over D-Bus).

It plays exactly the role the Helm One bike computer plays: discover a CSC
sensor, connect, subscribe to the CSC Measurement characteristic, and derive
cadence from the notification stream with the same arithmetic
(rpm = revs_delta * 1024 * 60 / time_delta, event times in 1/1024 s).

Usage:
    python3 csc_central.py                      # find + connect + 15 s of cadence
    python3 csc_central.py -s 30 --addr C0:DE:CA:DE:00:01
    python3 csc_central.py --cp-test            # also poke the SC Control Point
"""
import argparse
import sys
import time

import dbus
import dbus.mainloop.glib
from gi.repository import GLib

BLUEZ = "org.bluez"
OM_IFACE = "org.freedesktop.DBus.ObjectManager"
PROP_IFACE = "org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties"
DEV_IFACE = "org.bluez.Device1"
ADAPTER_IFACE = "org.bluez.Adapter1"
CHR_IFACE = "org.bluez.GattCharacteristic1"

UUID_CSC_MEAS = "00002a5b-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb"
UUID_CSC_FEAT = "00002a5c-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb"
UUID_CSC_LOC = "00002a5d-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb"
UUID_CSC_CP = "00002a55-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb"
UUID_BAT_LEVEL = "00002a19-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb"
UUID_BAS = "0000180f-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb"
UUID_CSC_SVC = "00001816-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb"


def objects(bus):
    return bus.call_blocking(BLUEZ, "/", OM_IFACE, "GetManagedObjects", "", [])


def find_adapter(objs):
    for path, ifaces in objs.items():
        if ADAPTER_IFACE in ifaces:
            return path
    raise SystemExit("no bluetooth adapter on this host")


def find_device(objs, addr):
    for path, ifaces in objs.items():
        if DEV_IFACE in ifaces and str(ifaces[DEV_IFACE].get("Address", "")).upper() == addr.upper():
            return path
    return None


def wait_for_device(bus, adapter, addr, timeout=15.0):
    dev = find_device(objects(bus), addr)
    if dev is not None:
        return dev

    print("scanning for %s ..." % addr)
    bus.call_blocking(BLUEZ, adapter, ADAPTER_IFACE, "StartDiscovery", "", [])
    deadline = time.time() + timeout
    try:
        while time.time() < deadline:
            time.sleep(0.5)
            dev = find_device(objects(bus), addr)
            if dev is not None:
                return dev
    finally:
        try:
            bus.call_blocking(BLUEZ, adapter, ADAPTER_IFACE, "StopDiscovery", "", [])
        except dbus.exceptions.DBusException:
            pass
    raise SystemExit("device %s not found" % addr)


def prop(bus, path, iface, name):
    return bus.call_blocking(BLUEZ, path, PROP_IFACE, "Get", "", [iface, name])


def children(objs, dev_path, iface):
    """Yield (path, props) of the device's objects exposing iface."""
    for path, ifaces in objs.items():
        if path.startswith(dev_path + "/") and iface in ifaces:
            yield path, ifaces[iface]


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("-a", "--addr", default="C0:DE:CA:DE:00:01")
    ap.add_argument("-s", "--seconds", type=float, default=15.0)
    ap.add_argument("--cp-test", action="store_true",
                    help="write the SC Control Point to check its error handling")
    ap.add_argument("--keep", action="store_true", help="stay connected at the end")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    dbus.mainloop.glib.DBusGMainLoop(set_as_default=True)
    bus = dbus.SystemBus()

    objs = objects(bus)
    adapter = find_adapter(objs)
    dev_path = wait_for_device(bus, adapter, args.addr)
    print("device path %s" % dev_path)

    dev = bus.get_object(BLUEZ, dev_path)
    dev_props = dbus.Interface(dev, PROP_IFACE)
    print("connect ...")
    dev_props.Set(DEV_IFACE, "Trusted", dbus.Boolean(True))
    dbus.Interface(dev, DEV_IFACE).Connect()

    deadline = time.time() + 15.0
    while time.time() < deadline:
        if bool(prop(bus, dev_path, DEV_IFACE, "ServicesResolved")):
            break
        time.sleep(0.2)
    else:
        raise SystemExit("services were not resolved in time")

    objs = objects(bus)
    services = {str(p.get("UUID", "")).lower(): p for p, _ in
                children(objs, dev_path, "org.bluez.GattService1")}
    if UUID_CSC_SVC not in services:
        raise SystemExit("no CSC service on the device!")
    print("CSC service found: %s" % services[UUID_CSC_SVC])

    chars = {}
    for path, props in children(objs, dev_path, CHR_IFACE):
        chars[str(props.get("UUID", "")).lower()] = (path, props)

    for uuid, label in ((UUID_CSC_FEAT, "feature"), (UUID_CSC_LOC, "location"),
                        (UUID_BAT_LEVEL, "battery")):
        if uuid not in chars:
            print("%-9s: (absent)" % label)
            continue
        path = chars[uuid][0]
        try:
            value = bytes(bus.call_blocking(BLUEZ, path, CHR_IFACE, "ReadValue", "", [{}]))
        except dbus.exceptions.DBusException as exc:
            print("%-9s: read failed: %s" % (label, exc.get_dbus_name()))
            continue
        if uuid == UUID_CSC_FEAT:
            feat = int.from_bytes(value, "little")
            print("%-9s: 0x%04x  wheel=%d crank=%d multi-location=%d" %
                  (label, feat, feat & 1, (feat >> 1) & 1, (feat >> 2) & 1))
        else:
            print("%-9s: %s" % (label, value.hex()))

    if UUID_CSC_MEAS not in chars:
        raise SystemExit("no CSC Measurement characteristic!")
    meas_path, meas_props = chars[UUID_CSC_MEAS]
    print("measurement: %s props=%s" % (meas_path, ",".join(meas_props.get("Flags", []))))

    if args.cp_test and UUID_CSC_CP in chars:
        # No indication subscription: the profile says the sensor must answer
        # with "CCC improperly configured" (0x81).
        try:
            bus.call_blocking(BLUEZ, chars[UUID_CSC_CP][0], CHR_IFACE, "WriteValue", "",
                              [dbus.Array([dbus.Byte(0x01), dbus.Byte(0), dbus.Byte(0),
                                           dbus.Byte(0), dbus.Byte(0)], signature="y"), {}])
            print("control point: write accepted (expected an error)")
        except dbus.exceptions.DBusException as exc:
            print("control point: write rejected with %s (CCC improper)" %
                  exc.get_dbus_message().split(":", 1)[-1].strip())

    state = {"revs": None, "time": None, "packets": 0, "rpms": []}

    def on_props(iface, changed, _invalidated, path=None):
        if iface != CHR_IFACE or path != meas_path or "Value" not in changed:
            return
        value = bytes(changed["Value"])
        state["packets"] += 1
        if len(value) < 5:
            print("packet too short: %s" % value.hex())
            return
        flags = value[0]
        off = 1
        wheel = None
        if flags & 0x01:
            wheel = (int.from_bytes(value[1:5], "little"), int.from_bytes(value[5:7], "little"))
            off += 6
        if not flags & 0x02:
            print("flags=0x%02x wheel=%s  (no crank data)" % (flags, wheel))
            return
        revs = int.from_bytes(value[off:off + 2], "little")
        evt = int.from_bytes(value[off + 2:off + 4], "little")
        rpm = None
        if state["revs"] is not None:
            drev = (revs - state["revs"]) & 0xffff
            dtime = (evt - state["time"]) & 0xffff
            if drev and dtime:
                rpm = drev * 1024 * 60 / dtime
                state["rpms"].append(rpm)
        state["revs"], state["time"] = revs, evt
        print("#%-3d flags=0x%02x revs=%-5d evt=%-5d  -> %s rpm" %
              (state["packets"], flags, revs, evt,
               ("%.1f" % rpm) if rpm is not None else "(baseline)"))

    bus.add_signal_receiver(on_props, signal_name="PropertiesChanged",
                            dbus_interface=PROP_IFACE, path_keyword="path")

    print("subscribing to notifications for %.0f s ..." % args.seconds)
    bus.call_blocking(BLUEZ, meas_path, CHR_IFACE, "StartNotify", "", [])

    loop = GLib.MainLoop()
    GLib.timeout_add(int(args.seconds * 1000), lambda: (loop.quit(), False)[1])
    try:
        loop.run()
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass

    try:
        bus.call_blocking(BLUEZ, meas_path, CHR_IFACE, "StopNotify", "", [])
    except dbus.exceptions.DBusException:
        pass

    rpms = state["rpms"]
    print("\n%d notifications, %d cadence samples" % (state["packets"], len(rpms)))
    if rpms:
        print("cadence: min %.1f  max %.1f  mean %.1f rpm" %
              (min(rpms), max(rpms), sum(rpms) / len(rpms)))

    if not args.keep:
        dbus.Interface(dev, DEV_IFACE).Disconnect()
    return 0 if rpms else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""串口转发枢纽（serial hub）：**一个独立小程序**，谁都能用它共享一个串口。

## 它是什么

一个进程独占串口，把所有读到的东西转发给挂在它上面的客户端；客户端也能把数据写回
串口。于是"一个串口、多个终端"成为可能：交互式终端、AI/脚本、别的串口工具，都通过
`/tmp` 里的那个 Unix 套接字和它说话。

**它自己会死**：最后一个客户端离开后 `--idle-timeout`（默认 5 s）秒，自己退出并把
套接字删掉 —— 所以"人都走了，`/tmp` 里那个文件就没了"是成立的，不需要谁去清理。

## 怎么用

```bash
# 前台起（默认套接字 /tmp/vela-serial-<串口名>.sock）
python3 serial_hub.py /dev/ttyACM0 --baud 1000000
python3 serial_hub.py /dev/ttyACM0 --reset      # 起来先补一次硬件复位（抓 SFBL 起）
python3 serial_hub.py /dev/ttyACM0 --no-idle-exit   # 别自杀（长驻）

# 然后任何工具连上去（vela_my_vendor_tools 的 monitor / monitor-ctl 就是这么用的）
python3 vela_my_vendor_tools.py monitor-ctl -p /dev/ttyACM0            # 第二个终端
python3 vela_my_vendor_tools.py monitor-ctl -p /dev/ttyACM0 --status    # 一行状态
```

## 协议（换任何语言都能接）

一行一个 JSON（UTF-8，`\n` 结尾）。请求 `{"op": …}`，应答 `{"ok": …}`；`attach`
之后服务端会持续推 `{"ev":"rx","b64":"…"}`。

| op | 作用 |
|----|------|
| `status` | `{ok, port, baud, open, released, clients, hub_pid}` |
| `rx` | 只读：环形缓冲全文（64 KiB） |
| `send` | `{text}` 或 `{hex}` 写进串口，`wait_ms`/`idle_ms` 内收集回显 |
| `tx` | `{b64}` 原始字节写进串口（二进制安全，按键级） |
| `attach` | `{replay}` 变成流式客户端：先回放最近 `replay` 字节，之后实时推送 |
| `release` / `acquire` | 让出串口给别的程序（如 sftool 烧录）/ 收回；`acquire` 可带 `pulse` |
| `pulse` | 只发一次硬件复位脉冲 |
| `shutdown` | 立即收工（关串口、删套接字） |

`release` 期间仍能应答（`status` 会说 `released: true`），且**不会**因为"没有客户端"
而自杀 —— 那是烧录窗口，收工要等 `acquire` 或者超时。

## 与 vela_my_vendor_tools 的关系

`monitor` 自己持有串口时不需要它；当**没有任何人持有**而又有工具想用（例如先跑的是
`monitor-ctl`），`vela_my_vendor_tools.py` 会自动把本程序拉起来当持有者。反过来，
本程序也可以先手工起，然后 `monitor` 会以客户端身份挂上来。

{"content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Drive the Helm One board console through the serial hub, reading replies from
an `attach` stream.

Workaround for a bug in serial_hub.py: the `send` op computes "new output" as
_rx[len(_rx):], and _rx is a bytearray trimmed to a 64 KiB ring - so once the
ring is saturated (a chatty board fills it in minutes) every `send` reports an
empty reply even though data is flowing.  Attaching gives a live stream that
does not depend on that offset.

  vela_nsh2.py -d 3 "test sensor scan 12" -d 20 "test sensor list"
"""
import argparse
import base64
import json
import re
import socket
import sys
import threading
import time

SOCK = "/tmp/vela-serial-ttyACM0.sock"


def connect():
    s = socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
    s.settimeout(30)
    s.connect(SOCK)
    return s


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("-s", "--sock", default=SOCK)
    ap.add_argument("-w", "--wait-ms", type=int, default=0)
    ap.add_argument("-k", "--keep", type=int, default=3, help="seconds to keep listening at the end")
    ap.add_argument("-q", "--quiet", action="store_true", help="drop the 1 Hz [radio] tick lines")
    ap.add_argument("cmd", nargs="*", help="one or more console commands")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    reader = connect()
    reader.sendall((json.dumps({"op": "attach", "replay": 0}) + "\n").encode())
    stop = threading.Event()
    drops = [0]

    def pump():
        buf = b""
        tick = re.compile(rb"\[radio\] tick")
        while not stop.is_set():
            try:
                chunk = reader.recv(65536)
            except (socket.timeout, OSError):
                break
            if not chunk:
                break
            buf += chunk
            while b"\n" in buf:
                line, buf = buf.split(b"\n", 1)
                if not line.strip():
                    continue
                try:
                    msg = json.loads(line.decode("utf-8", "replace"))
                except ValueError:
                    continue
                if msg.get("ev") != "rx":
                    continue
                text = base64.b64decode(msg["b64"]).decode("utf-8", "replace")
                if args.quiet:
                    kept = []
                    for ln in text.splitlines(True):
                        if tick.search(ln.encode("utf-8", "replace")):
                            drops[0] += 1
                        else:
                            kept.append(ln)
                    text = "".join(kept)
                    if not text:
                        continue
                sys.stdout.write(text)
                sys.stdout.flush()

    th = threading.Thread(target=pump, daemon=True)
    th.start()
    time.sleep(0.4)

    writer = connect()
    for cmd in args.cmd:
        sys.stdout.write("\n########## %s\n" % cmd)
        sys.stdout.flush()
        writer.sendall((json.dumps({"op": "send", "text": cmd, "wait_ms": args.wait_ms}) + "\n").encode())
        time.sleep(args.wait_ms / 1000.0 if args.wait_ms else 0)
        # give the board time to answer / finish scanning before the next command
        time.sleep(2.0)
        # a scan takes as long as it takes; the caller passes -w to cover it
        if args.wait_ms:
            continue

    if args.keep:
        sys.stdout.write("\n... listening %d s more\n" % args.keep)
        sys.stdout.flush()
        time.sleep(args.keep)

    stop.set()
    reader.close()
    writer.close()
    if drops[0]:
        sys.stdout.write("\n(dropped %d [radio] tick lines)\n" % drops[0])
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
